Edwards Lifesciences (NYSE&#58; EW) today reported financial results for the quarter ended March&#160;31, 2026.</font></div><div><font><br></font></div><div style="margin-bottom:3pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:11pt;font-weight:700;line-height:174%;text-decoration:underline">Highlights and Outlook</font></div><div style="padding-left:13.5pt;text-indent:-13.5pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:11pt;font-weight:400;line-height:174%">&#8226;</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:11pt;font-weight:400;line-height:174%;padding-left:9.65pt">Q1 sales grew 16.7% to $1.65 billion</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:7.15pt;font-weight:400;line-height:174%;position:relative;top:-3.85pt;vertical-align:baseline">1</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:11pt;font-weight:400;line-height:174%">, constant currency</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:7.15pt;font-weight:400;line-height:174%;position:relative;top:-3.85pt;vertical-align:baseline">2</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:11pt;font-weight:400;line-height:174%"> sales grew 12.7%</font></div><div style="padding-left:13.5pt;text-indent:-13.5pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:11pt;font-weight:400;line-height:174%">&#8226;</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:11pt;font-weight:400;line-height:174%;padding-left:9.65pt">Q1 TAVR sales grew 14.4% to $1.20 billion</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:7.15pt;font-weight:400;line-height:174%;position:relative;top:-3.85pt;vertical-align:baseline">1</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:11pt;font-weight:400;line-height:174%">&#59; constant currency</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:7.15pt;font-weight:400;line-height:174%;position:relative;top:-3.85pt;vertical-align:baseline">2</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:11pt;font-weight:400;line-height:174%"> sales grew 11.0%</font></div><div style="padding-left:13.5pt;text-indent:-13.5pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:11pt;font-weight:400;line-height:174%">&#8226;</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:11pt;font-weight:400;line-height:174%;padding-left:9.65pt">Q1 TMTT sales of $173 million</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:7.15pt;font-weight:400;line-height:174%;position:relative;top:-3.85pt;vertical-align:baseline">1,3</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:11pt;font-weight:400;line-height:174%">, driven by repair and replacement therapies</font></div><div style="padding-left:13.5pt;text-indent:-13.5pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:11pt;font-weight:400;line-height:174%">&#8226;</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:11pt;font-weight:400;line-height:174%;padding-left:9.65pt">Q1 EPS of $0.66</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:7.15pt;font-weight:400;line-height:174%;position:relative;top:-3.85pt;vertical-align:baseline">1</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:11pt;font-weight:400;line-height:174%">&#59; adjusted</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:7.15pt;font-weight:400;line-height:174%;position:relative;top:-3.85pt;vertical-align:baseline">2</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:11pt;font-weight:400;line-height:174%"> EPS of $0.78</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:7.15pt;font-weight:400;line-height:174%;position:relative;top:-3.85pt;vertical-align:baseline">1</font></div><div style="padding-left:13.5pt;text-indent:-13.5pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:11pt;font-weight:400;line-height:174%">&#8226;</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:11pt;font-weight:400;line-height:174%;padding-left:9.65pt">Raising FY 2026 constant currency</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:7.15pt;font-weight:400;line-height:174%;position:relative;top:-3.85pt;vertical-align:baseline">2</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:11pt;font-weight:400;line-height:174%"> sales growth guidance to 9% to 11% from 8% to 10%</font></div><div style="padding-left:13.5pt;text-indent:-13.5pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:11pt;font-weight:400;line-height:174%">&#8226;</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:11pt;font-weight:400;line-height:174%;padding-left:9.65pt">Raising FY 2026 adjusted</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:7.15pt;font-weight:400;line-height:174%;position:relative;top:-3.85pt;vertical-align:baseline">2</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:11pt;font-weight:400;line-height:174%"> EPS guidance midpoint&#59; new range of $2.95 to $3.05 from $2.90 to $3.05</font></div><div style="padding-left:13.5pt;text-indent:-13.5pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:11pt;font-weight:400;line-height:174%">&#8226;</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:11pt;font-weight:400;line-height:174%;padding-left:9.65pt">Renewed clinical focus on proactive disease management with differentiated SAPIEN TAVR</font></div><div style="padding-left:13.5pt;text-indent:-13.5pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:11pt;font-weight:400;line-height:174%">&#8226;</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:11pt;font-weight:400;line-height:174%;padding-left:9.65pt">Completed $500 million Accelerated Share Repurchase</font></div><div style="text-indent:4.5pt"><font><br></font></div><div style="text-indent:36pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:11pt;font-weight:400;line-height:174%">&#8220;Building on a year in 2025 marked by solid financial performance and strategic progress, we delivered another strong quarter in Q1, achieving 12.7% sales growth, which reflects the impact and durability of our focused strategy. We remain dedicated to solving large, urgent and complex patient needs and pursuing unique opportunities to innovate and lead in structural heart disease,&#8221; said Bernard Zovighian, Edwards&#8217; CEO. &#8220;Based on our first quarter performance, we are raising our financial guidance for 2026. We continue to pursue additional meaningful growth opportunities across our portfolio, and our financial strength and strategic clarity give us confidence in the future.&#8221;</font></div><div style="margin-top:6pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:11pt;font-weight:700;line-height:232%;text-decoration:underline">Transcatheter Aortic Valve Replacement (TAVR)</font></div><div style="text-indent:36pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:11pt;font-weight:400;line-height:174%">In the first quarter, the company reported TAVR sales of $1.2 billion, which grew 14.4% compared to the prior year, or 11.0% on a constant currency basis. SAPIEN growth in the U.S. was healthy, and it was even faster outside of the U.S. Edwards&#8217; global competitive position in the first quarter increased slightly year-over-year mainly due to the exit of a competitor in Europe. Average selling prices were stable globally. Based on Edwards&#8217; first quarter TAVR performance, the company is raising its full-year 2026 TAVR sales growth guidance to 7% to 9% from 6% to 8%.</font></div><div style="height:27pt;position:relative;width:100%"><div style="bottom:0;position:absolute;width:100%"><div><font><br></font></div></div></div><hr style="page-break-after:always"><div style="min-height:45pt;width:100%"><div style="text-align:center"><font><br></font></div><div style="text-align:right"><font><br></font></div><div><font><br></font></div></div><div style="text-indent:36pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:11pt;font-weight:400;line-height:174%">Recent clinical trial results on long-term TAVR performance continue to support patient treatment with SAPIEN TAVR. The company is encouraged by the broader momentum that the EARLY TAVR study data has generated across the clinical community for both symptomatic and asymptomatic patients. There has been a shift toward proactive disease management, with an increased focus on evaluation and intentional referral of patients with severe aortic stenosis earlier in the disease pathway. This evolution in patient management, combined with a large and growing body of long-term SAPIEN outcomes data, reinforces the company&#8217;s confidence in the durable, multi-year growth opportunity ahead. Later this year, results of the PROGRESS trial studying patients with moderate AS will be presented at the TCT conference.</font></div><div style="text-indent:36pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:11pt;font-weight:400;line-height:174%">In the U.S., the Centers for Medicare &#38; Medicaid Services (CMS) is conducting the process to reconsider the National Coverage Determination (NCD) for TAVR. This decision has the potential to improve timely access to lifesaving TAVR therapy. In&#8239;Europe,&#8239;first quarter results demonstrated continued strong commercial execution and sustained physician demand for the SAPIEN platform. Updated guidelines&#8239;from the European&#8239;Society of Cardiology and&#8239;the&#8239;European Association&#8239;for&#8239;Cardio-Thoracic&#8239;Surgery&#8239;are reshaping clinical discussions around proactive disease management and reinforcing the role of TAVR for a broader patient population. Outside of Europe, sales growth was strong across multiple geographies, including Japan, driven by procedural growth and adoption of our SAPIEN 3 Ultra RESILIA platform. </font></div><div style="margin-top:6pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:11pt;font-weight:700;line-height:232%;text-decoration:underline">Transcatheter Mitral and Tricuspid Therapies (TMTT)</font></div><div style="text-indent:36pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:11pt;font-weight:400;line-height:174%">First quarter TMTT sales of $173 million were driven by the company&#8217;s unique portfolio of repair and replacement therapies to treat mitral and tricuspid diseases. Globally, mitral and tricuspid procedures grew in the estimated double digits, with Edwards&#8217; sales growing at a higher rate.</font></div><div style="text-indent:36pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:11pt;font-weight:400;line-height:174%">In tricuspid, at the recent American College of Cardiology (ACC) scientific session, two-year TRISCEND II data were presented, demonstrating significantly lower all-cause mortality with EVOQUE when accounting for patient crossover. The company continues to increase patient access to transcatheter tricuspid valve replacement and drive further adoption of EVOQUE by expanding into new centers.</font></div><div style="text-indent:36pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:11pt;font-weight:400;line-height:174%">Adoption of Edwards&#8217; PASCAL transcatheter edge-to-edge repair (TEER) technology continues to increase, driven by physician enthusiasm for its unique design and differentiated outcomes, and underscored by the significant needs of these patients. The company&#8217;s progress on the PASCAL pipeline remains on track, with a next-generation technology expected in Q4 for both mitral and tricuspid patients in the U.S. and Europe. In addition, Edwards expects the launch of PASCAL in the U.S. for tricuspid patients in Q4 of this year, which will expand the population of patients that can benefit from this impactful technology.</font></div><div style="text-indent:36pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:11pt;font-weight:400;line-height:174%">The recent FDA approval of SAPIEN M3 expands Edwards&#8217; mitral portfolio in the U.S. The company&#8217;s commercial experience, while early, validates the need for this mitral replacement solution for </font></div><div style="height:27pt;position:relative;width:100%"><div style="bottom:0;position:absolute;width:100%"><div style="text-align:center"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">2</font></div></div></div><hr style="page-break-after:always"><div style="min-height:45pt;width:100%"><div style="text-align:center"><font><br></font></div><div style="text-align:right"><font><br></font></div><div><font><br></font></div></div><div><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:11pt;font-weight:400;line-height:174%">patients who are not well-suited for mitral TEER. Physician feedback on patient outcomes and procedural experience with SAPIEN M3 has been positive.</font></div><div style="text-indent:36pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:11pt;font-weight:400;line-height:174%">The strong and increasing utilization of Edwards&#8217; differentiated therapies &#8211; EVOQUE, PASCAL and SAPIEN M3 &#8211; combined with double-digit mitral and tricuspid procedure volumes globally positions Edwards for continued growth.</font></div><div style="margin-top:6pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:11pt;font-weight:700;line-height:232%;text-decoration:underline">Surgical</font></div><div style="text-indent:36pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:11pt;font-weight:400;line-height:174%">In Surgical, first quarter global sales of $276 million increased 10.1% compared to the prior year, or 5.9% on a constant currency basis, driven by continued adoption of the company&#8217;s RESILIA therapies that offer extended durability. INSPIRIS adoption continues to increase globally. The KONECT aortic valved conduit, which facilitates Bentall procedures for patients in need, recently launched in Europe with strong adoption. With the launch of MITRIS in additional markets around the world, uptake of this technology in surgical mitral valve replacement procedures was strong.</font></div><div style="text-indent:36pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:11pt;font-weight:400;line-height:174%">The 10-year data from the company&#8217;s COMMENCE trial, studying the long-term durability of its best-in-class RESILIA tissue, will be presented at the upcoming American Association for Thoracic Surgery (AATS) conference. Edwards continues to expect that its surgical tricuspid valve, TRIFORMIS, will launch in the second half of the year. The company&#8217;s surgical Left Atrial Appendage Closure, or LAAC, program is on track for preliminary introduction later this year. </font></div><div style="margin-top:6pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:11pt;font-weight:700;line-height:232%;text-decoration:underline">Additional Financial Results</font></div><div style="text-indent:36pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:11pt;font-weight:400;line-height:174%">For the quarter, gross profit margin was 78.0%, or 78.2% adjusted, compared to 78.7% in the same period last year. The year-over-year change was driven by a weakening dollar as well as additional manufacturing expenses related to the expansion of new therapies. The company is maintaining its full-year 78% to 79% gross margin guidance.</font></div><div style="text-indent:36pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:11pt;font-weight:400;line-height:174%">Selling, general and administrative expenses in the first quarter were $522 million, or 31.7% of sales, compared to 33.0% of sales in the prior year. This was in line with the company&#8217;s expectations and reflects continued funding of resources Edwards provides to support patient care as well as a higher translation of the company&#8217;s OUS expense base from the weakening dollar. Research and Development (R&#38;D) expenses in the first quarter were $263 million, or 16.0% of sales, compared to 18.0% in the prior year. This decrease in R&#38;D as a percentage of sales and increase in total expense reflects Edwards&#8217; strong top-line growth as well as strategic prioritization of investments in its expanding structural heart portfolio. The company continues to expect R&#38;D expense as a percentage of sales to be approximately 17% in 2026.</font></div><div style="text-indent:36pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:11pt;font-weight:400;line-height:174%">Operating profit margin in the first quarter of 29.0%, or 31.4% adjusted, was in line with the company&#8217;s expectation for the quarter. Adjusted EPS was $0.78 and benefited from solid operational performance and planned phasing of strategic investments during the course of the year. In 2026, Edwards expects full-year operating profit margin to be at the high end of the company&#8217;s original 28% to </font></div><div style="height:27pt;position:relative;width:100%"><div style="bottom:0;position:absolute;width:100%"><div style="text-align:center"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">3</font></div></div></div><hr style="page-break-after:always"><div style="min-height:45pt;width:100%"><div style="text-align:center"><font><br></font></div><div style="text-align:right"><font><br></font></div><div><font><br></font></div></div><div><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:11pt;font-weight:400;line-height:174%">29% guidance range, resulting in approximately 150 basis points of constant currency operating margin expansion for the full year.</font></div><div style="text-indent:36pt"><font style="background-color:#ffffff;color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:11pt;font-weight:400;line-height:174%">Cash and cash equivalents were approximately </font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:11pt;font-weight:400;line-height:174%">$2.4 billion</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:174%"> </font><font style="background-color:#ffffff;color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:11pt;font-weight:400;line-height:174%">as of March 31, 2026. Total debt was approximately $600 million.</font></div><div style="text-indent:36pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:11pt;font-weight:400;line-height:174%">Also during the quarter, the company entered into an Accelerated Share Repurchase agreement to buy back $500 million in shares. Edwards has approximately $1.5 billion remaining under its share repurchase authorization.</font></div><div style="margin-top:6pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:11pt;font-weight:700;line-height:232%;text-decoration:underline">Outlook</font></div><div style="text-indent:36pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:11pt;font-weight:400;line-height:174%">Due to stronger-than-expected first quarter results, Edwards is raising its full-year 2026 sales growth rate guidance to 9% to 11% from 8% to 10% and TAVR product group sales growth rate guidance to 7% to 9% from 6% to 8%. Edwards now expects total company sales of $6.5 to $6.9 billion, and TAVR sales of $4.7 to $5.0 billion at current exchange rates. The company continues to expect $740 to $780 million in TMTT sales and mid-single-digit sales growth in Surgical in 2026. In addition, Edwards is raising the midpoint of its full-year adjusted EPS guidance with a new range of $2.95 to $3.05 from $2.90 to $3.05. For the second quarter of 2026, the company projects total sales to be between $1.66 and $1.74 billion and adjusted EPS of $0.70 to $0.76.</font></div><div style="margin-top:6pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:11pt;font-weight:700;line-height:232%;text-decoration:underline">About Edwards Lifesciences</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:11pt;font-weight:400;line-height:232%">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;</font></div><div style="text-indent:36pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:11pt;font-weight:400;line-height:174%">Edwards Lifesciences is the leading global structural heart innovation company, driven by a passion to improve patient lives. Through breakthrough technologies, world-class evidence and partnerships with clinicians and healthcare stakeholders, our employees are inspired by our patient-focused culture to deliver life-changing innovations to those who need them most. Discover more at www.edwards.com and follow us on LinkedIn, Facebook, Instagram and YouTube.</font></div><div style="margin-top:6pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:11pt;font-weight:700;line-height:232%;text-decoration:underline">Conference Call and Webcast Information</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:11pt;font-weight:400;line-height:232%">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;</font></div><div style="text-indent:36pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:11pt;font-weight:400;line-height:174%">The company will be hosting a conference call today at 2&#58;00&#160;p.m. PT to discuss its first quarter results.&#160;To participate in the conference call, dial (877) 704-2848 or (201) 389-0893. style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">6</font></div></div></div><div id="ie13c198afe0748d5bd96e7f1e94958c3_10"></div><hr style="page-break-after:always"><div style="min-height:40.5pt;width:100%"><div style="text-align:center"><font><br></font></div><div style="text-align:right"><font><br></font></div><div><font><br></font></div></div><div><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:9.5pt;font-weight:700;line-height:120%">EDWARDS LIFESCIENCES CORPORATION</font></div><div><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:9.5pt;font-weight:700;line-height:120%">Non-GAAP Financial Information</font></div><div><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:9.5pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">&#160;</font></div><div><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:9.5pt;font-weight:400;line-height:112%">To supplement the consolidated financial results prepared in accordance with Generally Accepted Accounting Principles (&#8220;GAAP&#8221;), the Company uses non-GAAP historical financial measures. Management makes adjustments to the GAAP measures for items (both charges and gains) that (a) do not reflect the core operational activities of the Company, (b) are commonly adjusted within the Company&#8217;s industry to enhance comparability of the Company&#8217;s financial results with those of its peer group, or (c) are inconsistent in amount or frequency between periods (albeit such items are monitored and controlled with equal diligence relative to core operations). The Company uses the terms &#8220;adjusted&#8221; and &#8220;constant currency&#8221; when referring to non-GAAP sales from continuing operations and sales growth information, respectively, which excludes currency exchange rate fluctuations and newly acquired products. The Company uses the term &#8220;adjusted&#8221; to also exclude certain litigation expenses, amortization of intangible assets, a gain on remeasurement of previously held interest upon acquisition, loss on impairment, and separation costs.</font></div><div><font><br></font></div><div><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:9.5pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">Management uses non-GAAP financial measures internally for strategic decision making, forecasting future results, and evaluating current performance. These non-GAAP financial measures are used in addition to, and in conjunction with, results presented in accordance with GAAP and reflect an additional way of viewing aspects of the Company's operations by investors that, when viewed with its GAAP results, provide a more complete understanding of factors and trends affecting the Company's business and facilitate comparability to historical periods.  </font></div><div><font><br></font></div><div><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:9.5pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">Non-GAAP financial measures are not prepared in accordance with GAAP&#59; therefore, the information is not necessarily comparable to other companies and should be considered as a supplement to, and not as a substitute for, or superior to, the corresponding measures calculated in accordance with GAAP. A reconciliation of non-GAAP historical financial measures to the most comparable GAAP measure is provided in the tables below.</font></div><div><font><br></font></div><div><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:9.5pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">Fluctuations in currency exchange rates impact the comparative results and sales growth rates of the Company's underlying business. Management believes that excluding the impact of currency exchange rate fluctuations from its sales growth provides investors a more useful comparison to historical financial results. The impact of the fluctuations has been detailed in the &#8220;Reconciliation of Sales by Product Group and Region.&#8221;  </font></div><div><font><br></font></div><div><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:9.5pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">Guidance for sales and sales growth rates is provided on a &#8220;constant currency basis,&#8221; and projections for diluted earnings per share, net income and growth, gross profit margin, and taxes are also provided on a non-GAAP basis, as adjusted, for the items identified above due to the inherent difficulty in forecasting such items without unreasonable efforts. The Company is not able to provide a reconciliation of the non-GAAP guidance to comparable GAAP measures due to the unknown effect, timing, and potential significance of special charges or gains, and management's inability to forecast charges associated with future transactions and initiatives. </font></div><div><font><br></font></div><div><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:9.5pt;font-weight:700;line-height:120%;text-decoration:underline">The items described below are adjustments to the GAAP financial results in the reconciliations that follow&#58;</font></div><div><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:9.5pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">&#160;</font></div><div><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:9.5pt;font-weight:700;line-height:120%">Certain Litigation Expenses</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:9.5pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%"> - The Company incurred certain litigation expenses of $37.1 million and $10.9&#160;million in the first quarter of 2026 and 2025, respectively. Such expenses relate to intellectual property litigation, settlements, contingencies, and external legal costs.</font></div><div><font><br></font></div><div><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:9.5pt;font-weight:700;line-height:120%">Amortization of Intangible Assets</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:9.5pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%"> - The Company recorded amortization expense related to developed technology and patents in the amount of $3.3 million and $1.4&#160;million in the first quarter of 2026 and 2025, respectively.</font></div><div><font><br></font></div><div><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:9.5pt;font-weight:700;line-height:120%">Separation Costs</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Calibri',sans-serif;font-size:9.5pt;font-weight:700;line-height:120%"> </font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Calibri',sans-serif;font-size:9.5pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">- </font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:9.5pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">The Company recorded expenses of $4.2&#160;million in the first quarter of 2025, related to consulting, legal, tax, and other professional advisory services related to the sale of Critical Care.</font></div><div><font><br></font></div><div><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:9.5pt;font-weight:700;line-height:120%">Gain on Remeasurement of Previously Held Interest Upon Acquisition</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:9.5pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%"> - The Company recorded a $65.2&#160;million gain in the first quarter of 2026 to remeasure its previously held interest upon acquisition of an investee.</font></div><div><font><br></font></div><div><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:9.5pt;font-weight:700;line-height:112%">Loss on Impairment</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:9.5pt;font-weight:400;line-height:112%"> - The Company recorded loss on impairment of $123.6 million in the first quarter of 2026 ($99.0 million net of tax adjustment), due to the carrying amount of one of its VIE investments not being recoverable.</font></div><div><font><br></font></div><div><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:9.5pt;font-weight:700;line-height:120%">Provision for Income Taxes</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:9.5pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%"> - The income tax impacts of the expenses and gains discussed above are based upon the items' forecasted effect upon the Company's full-year effective tax rate. Adjustments to forecasted items unrelated to the expenses and gains above, as well as impacts related to interim reporting, will have an effect on the income tax impact of these items in subsequent
